metadata.title: Certified Weil Positivity at L = 4/5: Two-Sided Bounds, Parity Separation, and Cutoff Diagnostics
metadata.description:
For the Weil explicit-formula quadratic form restricted to test functions supported in a compact window [-L, L] with L = 4/5, this technical note reports a computer-assisted two-sided bound on its spectral infimum in one fixed normalization: 1.41e-17 ≤ lambda_Q(4/5) ≤ 1.9014e-17.

The lower bound comes from a frequency-cutoff comparison at T = 400, reduced to a 440-dimensional Legendre block whose positive definiteness is verified by a preconditioned congruence in Arb ball arithmetic, together with a super-exponentially small complement estimate and a Schur-type coupling bound; both parity sectors are certified. The upper bound is the Rayleigh quotient of the original form at one explicit even rational test function, evaluated in the time domain through the autocorrelation and a compact archimedean identity, so no oscillatory frequency tail is integrated. A separate certificate gives lambda_Q,odd ≥ 2.3e-17, which exceeds the upper bound and therefore shows that the even infimum determines lambda_Q. Diagnostics at cutoffs T in {200, 400, 800} measure the discarded exterior contribution and bound the gain available from a larger cutoff.

All constants are published as midpoint-radius enclosures with a cold verifier, together with the exact rational input vectors and the code that produced them. An appendix records the errors found during the work, several of which produced plausible wrong numbers rather than failures.

Scope. This is a computation at a single window. It establishes no arithmetic estimate, no statement about the location of any zero of the Riemann zeta function, no verified range of zeros, no result at any larger support, and nothing about the Riemann hypothesis. The finite-reduction strategy is taken from arXiv:2608.24827v2 and credited there; parity decoupling of the window form is likewise not new. The computation inherits its zeta-window normalization, geometric-side assembly, pole conventions and closed-form evaluator from the author's earlier sensitivity note (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23250932), and its even/odd pole signs were checked entrywise against that assembly in the author's real-zero parity note (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23624161); neither of those results is an input to the lower bound proved here. This is a technical note, not peer-reviewed research.
